summary:
LunaVector is an exploratory lunar mission-planning application designed to help users compare potential landing locations near the Moon’s south pole based on sunlight availability and direct-to-Earth visibility.

The application combines Sun and Earth position observations from NASA JPL Horizons with elevation data from NASA’s Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA). Using these datasets, LunaVector estimates how surrounding lunar terrain can obstruct sunlight and communication lines of sight.

Our prototype compares two illustrative locations at 89°S latitude over November 14–20, 2026. It provides interactive visualizations, hourly visibility estimates, terrain-horizon analysis, and sensitivity testing to help users understand important mission-design trade-offs.

LunaVector makes complex lunar environmental data more accessible to students, educators, researchers, and early-stage mission planners. The results are preliminary and intended for exploration rather than flight-qualified landing-site certification.
details:
LunaVector — Project Details

What does LunaVector do?

LunaVector is an exploratory lunar mission-planning application that helps users compare potential landing locations near the Moon's south pole. It focuses on two important challenges: sunlight availability and direct visibility of Earth for communication.

How does it work?

LunaVector combines Sun and Earth position observations from NASA JPL Horizons with elevation data from NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA).

The prototype compares two illustrative locations at 89°S latitude, separated by 90° longitude, using hourly observations from November 14–20, 2026.

It provides interactive charts, visibility percentages, terrain-horizon analysis, and comparisons between unobstructed and terrain-adjusted visibility.

In our demonstration, the terrain model estimates sunlight visibility of 51.7% at Site A and 40.0% at Site B. Earth-center visibility is estimated at 23.4% and 15.2%, respectively.

Technology used

The application was developed using Python, Streamlit, NumPy, Pandas, Plotly, Rasterio, and PyProj. It uses NASA JPL Horizons observations and NASA LOLA lunar elevation data.

What makes LunaVector useful?

LunaVector brings astronomical observations and lunar terrain analysis into one accessible interface. Instead of examining separate datasets, users can compare candidate locations and understand how nearby terrain may affect sunlight and communication opportunities.

The tool is intended for students, educators, researchers, and early-stage mission planners.

Limitations and future improvements

LunaVector is an exploratory prototype, not a certified landing-site selection system. Its terrain calculations require independent geospatial validation. Future improvements include more accurate terrain modeling, additional landing locations, solar-power estimation, communication link budgets, and landing-hazard analysis.

Our goal is to make lunar mission-planning concepts easier to explore, understand, and evaluate.
